# Independent candidate fixtures

These fixtures contain synthetic data. They were generated by tools independent of NYRA FWLab.

| File | Generator | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zip-fake-eocd.zip` | Python standard-library `zipfile` | `29dc1bf32a352abbba63d1dcb46895e9a1f4da06b47b929fc42fb92f691a2317` |
| `synthetic-fdt.dtb` | DTC 1.7.0 | `03b66a6c2e6f7f30dd1795483bd000e35f8e0f2280e1f8929dbd85fb1b952ba8` |
| `synthetic-ubi-ec.bin` | mtd-utils 2.2.0 | `e00087afa04e2a07f8b554cf59916926cefc022b246c1f1713031fc12e83f276` |

The ZIP has one stored member called `payload.bin` with timestamp 2024-01-01 00:00:00. Its contents are `b"fixture\0" + fake * 3 + b"end"`, where `fake = b"PK\x05\x06" + bytes(18)`. The archive comment also contains `fake`. The member and the comment exercise different ZIP end-record lookups.

Compile this source with `dtc -I dts -O dtb -o synthetic-fdt.dtb fixture.dts`.

```dts
/dts-v1/;
/ {
    compatible = "nyra-fwlab,synthetic-fixture";
    model = "NYRA FWLab synthetic DTB fixture";
};
```

The UBI fixture is the first 64 bytes of an image of an empty directory. Use `mkfs.ubifs -r empty-root -m 2048 -e 126976 -c 32 -j 1MiB -o empty.ubifs`, followed by `ubinize -m 2048 -p 128KiB -s 512 -O 2048 -Q 460348186 -o empty.ubi ubinize.ini`.

```ini
[ubifs]
mode=ubi
image=empty.ubifs
vol_id=0
vol_type=dynamic
vol_name=rootfs
vol_flags=autoresize
```

## Regression fixtures for archive classification and SquashFS tables

| File | Generator | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tiny.squashfs` | `mksquashfs` 4.6.1 | `f55ce1d0598fe79598653118f12388c3a4366ef24d70491c77569595e72db767` |
| `zip-bzip2-member.zip` | Python 3.12 `zipfile` | `531c1e3e75c51d19cded1f51530adb1db5704adaa81e77547f49cdb12c9efe34` |
| `zip-nested-stored.zip` | Python 3.12 `zipfile` | `c7aafed708823cf71719c0c6e6b61b30759be647896a8e4a25c4272cbf3d3b7f` |
| `zip-zip64-member.zip` | Python 3.12 `zipfile` | `f7aa9ec562c11191b58dcfd1996dd9c6ba3e1f30fbbf3bf7fea85c3545e5186d` |
| `tar-repeated-members.tar` | GNU tar 1.35 | `f69c813c2aae090927c6b7b23cddb1a0a54fe1d5b9538cd033b84bafc5f5e324` |

`tiny.squashfs` holds one 13-byte file, `hello.txt`, and `unsquashfs -ll` lists it:

```bash
mksquashfs tree tiny.squashfs -comp gzip -noappend -nopad -quiet -no-progress -all-time 0 -mkfs-time 0 -all-root -no-xattrs -b 4096
```

The three ZIP files are written with `ZipInfo` dates of 2024-01-01 and the `zipfile.ZIP_BZIP2`, `ZIP_STORED` and `ZIP_STORED` methods. `zip-nested-stored.zip` stores a complete ZIP as its only member, `firmware/inner.zip`. `zip-zip64-member.zip` is written with `force_zip64=True`, so its records carry ZIP64 marker values. `unzip -t` verifies all three. The TAR has two regular members that are both called `header`:

```bash
printf 'first\n' > header && tar -b 1 --format=gnu --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='2024-01-01 00:00:00' -cf tar-repeated-members.tar header
printf 'second\n' > header && tar -b 1 --format=gnu --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='2024-01-01 00:00:00' -rf tar-repeated-members.tar header
```
